name: TS3A27518ERTWR
title: 6-channel 1:2 multiplexer/demultiplexer (qSPI, SDIO) with IEC level-4 ESD and 1.8 V logic inputs
summary: Six bidirectional single-pole double-throw switches for 1.65 V to 3.6 V, each joining COM to NC or NO. IN1 sets switches 1 to 3 and IN2 sets switches 4 to 6; EN high opens every path. The control inputs have 1.8 V thresholds and accept up to 3.6 V, and the paths go high impedance when VCC is 0 V. Built to fan one six-wire SD, SDIO, MMC or qSPI port out to two devices.
key_figures: 4.4 Ω typ, 6.2 Ω max at VCC = 3 V, 25°C
0.04 µA typ, 3 µA max at VCC = 3.6 V

circuits.description: A baseband or applications processor's six-line SDIO port (CMD, CLK and four data lines) reaches either an SD/MMC memory card or an SDIO peripheral such as a Bluetooth, WLAN or DTV module. The port lines enter COM1 to COM6; NC1 to NC6 go to the card and NO1 to NO6 to the peripheral. The processor drives IN1, IN2 and EN. Switch, processor, card and peripheral share one VCC.

circuits.title: Figure 9-2. qSPI Expander Application Block Diagram
circuits.description: One processor qSPI port shared between two qSPI devices. The six port lines (four data, clock and chip select) enter COM1 to COM6; with IN1 and IN2 high they reach device 1 through NO1 to NO6, with both low they reach device 2 through NC1 to NC6. The processor drives IN1, IN2 and EN from its control logic. A 0.1 µF capacitor decouples VCC, which shares the processor's VDD rail.

equations.name: Bandwidth
equations.expr: BW = f at which ON-channel gain is 3 dB below its DC gain

operation.text: Two banks of three SPDT switches. IN1 moves switches 1, 2 and 3 together and IN2 moves switches 4, 5 and 6 together: a low control input connects each COM to its NC terminal, a high one connects it to NO. With EN high every switch is open and all terminals are high impedance, whatever IN1 and IN2 are.
Every path conducts in both directions and passes digital or analog signals up to VCC; NC, NO and COM can each be an input or an output. The analog range is 0 V to 3.6 V.

IN1, IN2 and EN have 1.8 V logic thresholds and also work with 2.5 V and 3.3 V logic. They tolerate 3.6 V regardless of VCC. Unused digital inputs are tied to VCC or GND, and TI recommends a pull-up to VCC or pull-down to GND on each IN pin so a floating input cannot leave the switch in an unwanted position.
With VCC = 0 V every switch path is high impedance.

No external components are needed for operation. TI recommends terminating unused signal pins to ground through 50 Ω so signals are not reflected into the part. The N.C. pin may be grounded or left without a trace. On the RTW package the thermal pad connects to ground.

Bring VCC up before any signal is applied to NO, NC or COM, and stay inside the absolute maximum ratings. Bypassing is optional but improves noise margin and keeps switching noise off the supply; 0.1 µF from VCC to GND suits most uses.
Place the VCC bypass capacitor (0603 on the WQFN layout) as close to the VCC pin as possible and keep traces short to limit loading. Connect the RTW thermal pad to ground.

Switching-time, break-before-make and charge-injection figures use pulse generators with PRR ≤ 10 MHz, ZO = 50 Ω, tr < 5 ns and tf < 5 ns, and the load capacitance CL counts the probe and fixture. Bandwidth, OFF isolation and crosstalk are measured on a network analyzer with 0 dBm source power (632 mV p-p into 50 Ω) and 350 mV DC bias, with 50 Ω source and load. THD uses a 600 Ω audio analyzer with VSOURCE = VCC p-p from 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

OFF leakage is measured at a terminal with its path open; ON leakage at a terminal with its path closed and the far side left open. Capacitance is measured at NO, COM and the control inputs with VBIAS = VCC or GND, in both switch states. Crosstalk is coupling from an ON channel into an OFF one (NC1 to NO1); adjacent crosstalk is coupling between two neighbouring ON channels (NC1 to NC2). ICC is the static supply current with the control inputs at VCC or GND.
A Q100-qualified automotive version is sold as TS3A27518E-Q1.
